sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Lee County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Lee County Clerk and Recorder, whose office is one flight upstairs at the Old Lee County Courthouse, 112 E Second Street, Dixon. The staff there also handle vital records, assumed names, elections and delinquent taxes. Call 815-288-3309 or mail to P.O. Box 329, Dixon, IL 61021. Counter hours are 8 until half past four on weekdays, except legal holidays.

The county has 15,027 housing units, and 90.5% of residents had not moved in the prior year. People rarely leave, so a lot of local deeds come from inheritances, trusts and estates. Those files take more care.

Bring the vesting deed with you. Staff will not write a legal description for you. Copy it exactly from an earlier deed or a title report.

The standard price for a warranty deed, quitclaim deed, mortgage release or similar paper is $88. If the document is exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee, the charge is $69. The fee schedule took effect July 1, 2023 under 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.1. A state act signed in February 2023 added $9 to the Rental Housing Support fee starting that July 1.

Pay with cash or check. The counter does not take debit or credit cards. Include a self-addressed stamped envelope, and send an original or certified copy, never a plain photocopy. Copies of a veteran's discharge are free. Transfer tax is a separate charge, covered below.

Papers that follow the county's layout rules pay the standard fee, and anything that breaks them is charged $97. The rules:

  • Separate 8.5 by 11 inch sheets, unbound and not on a continuous form, with any attached graphic no larger than 11 by 17 inches.
  • Black ink that reads clearly, whether handwritten, typed or printed. Dates and signatures can be another color if they copy cleanly.
  • White stock, 20-pound weight or heavier, and leave a half inch of blank margin all the way around.
  • An empty 3 by 5 inch box in the top right corner of page one.
  • Nothing stapled or taped onto a page, though sheets can be stapled to each other.

Nobody at the recorder's counter or on its phone line can offer legal advice, write a legal description or run a title search. Take the description from your vesting deed or ask the title company, and let an attorney draft anything that transfers ownership.

sections.h2: Is a Plat Act affidavit part of a Lee County deed?
sections.html:
Almost always. Each deed needs a plat act affidavit or a stated exemption. Deeds inside the Woodhaven Lakes subdivision are the one exception, and the county's posted form for them declares the transfer exempt from the Illinois Plat Act (765 ILCS 205), with check boxes for the reason, for example a conveyance that leaves the parcel whole.

Deeds often get returned for lack of this affidavit. Selling only part of a lot or field? See the assessment office and a surveyor before anyone drafts, since dividing land is where the exemption breaks down.

sections.h2: Illinois transfer tax and the declaration
sections.html:
The state charges fifty cents on every $500 of value, rounding a partial $500 up, based on the number written on the declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). If the deed passes the property subject to a mortgage, that loan balance does not count toward the value. Counties collect the tax by selling revenue stamps (35 ILCS 200/31-15).

The declaration needs a signature from one seller and one buyer at minimum, or from their attorneys or agents. Deliver it with the deed, or inside 3 business days of the transfer if that comes first (35 ILCS 200/31-25). It asks about price, parcel number, legal description, deed type, address, improvements, any homestead exemptions on the latest bill, and whether the buyer and seller are related or the sale was compulsory.

Some deeds owe nothing: tax deeds, deeds with consideration under $100, and deeds handed to a lender in foreclosure or in place of it (35 ILCS 200/31-45). Several still need a declaration. The Clerk and Recorder can tell you whether a local charge applies besides the state tax.

Staff keep the declaration apart from the deed. They note the deed's document number on it and send it to the chief county assessment officer within 30 days, and that office adds the assessed value and sends it to the Illinois Department of Revenue (35 ILCS 200/31-30). This is how assessment staff learn a Lee County parcel sold and for how much.

An accurate form protects both sides. It also affects the seller's homestead exemption: the credit carries through the assessment year in which you sell, and the next owner may be asked to apply for the year after (35 ILCS 200/15-175).

E-recording is open only to approved submitters, from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. The county names four partners:

  • Corporation Service Company, at erecording.com
  • eRecording Partners Network, at goepn.com
  • Simplifile, at simplifile.com
  • Hopdox, at hopdox.com

Most title companies and closing attorneys file through one of these on the day of closing. A family transfer without a title company can go by mail, paper original plus check plus stamped return envelope, or be handed in at the counter. If you file on paper, call ahead so you know the exact total before you write the check.

sections.h2: Checks before the deed goes in
sections.html:
First look up the parcel on the county's property tax inquiry site and confirm who is the owner of record. Next, phone the Treasurer at 815-288-4477 and ask whether any year is unpaid or sold. When the buyer's title search turns up mortgages, liens or judgments, each has to be released of record or paid off at closing.

Inherited property adds steps. Whoever really holds title must sign as grantor, and that may be a personal representative who brings court papers. Repairs, tenants and back taxes do not change how recording works. They change who pays what at the closing table. A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but the deed, declaration and fees stay the same.

A simple checklist for the counter: the signed and notarized deed, the signed transfer declaration, the plat act affidavit or exemption statement, the right fee by check or cash, and a return envelope. Calling ahead on anything unusual saves a second trip to Dixon.

faqs.q: What is the fee for a standard deed in Lee County?
faqs.a: It is $88, or $69 for a document exempt from the Rental Housing Support fee. Six or more parcel numbers, or breaking the layout rules, raises it to $97.

faqs.q: Does the Lee County recorder take credit cards?
faqs.a: No, only cash or check at the counter. Electronic filers use one of four approved partners.

faqs.q: How is Illinois transfer tax calculated?
faqs.a: Fifty cents per $500 of value, rounding up (35 ILCS 200/31-10). A loan the buyer assumes is excluded if the deed says the transfer is subject to it.

faqs.q: Does every Lee County deed need a plat affidavit?
faqs.a: All but deeds in the Woodhaven Lakes subdivision. The affidavit or a stated exemption is required, and the county website has the form.

faqs.q: When can a title company e-record in Lee County?
faqs.a: Filing is open from 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. to approved submitters only. Those are Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and Hopdox.
